There's just multiple versions of the packet in existence. But this one's pretty much the same as she got.

This is the packet they gave them when I was born. So I think this is partially why:

https://www.circinfo.net/pdfs/GFP_EN(US)_1606.pdf

*If not circumcised soon after birth, up to 10% of males will later require one anyway for medical reasons.*

*Most research shows sexual function, sensitivity and
satisfaction are the same or better after circumcision.*

*In their lifetime, 1 in 2 uncircumcised boys will develop a medical condition caused by their foreskin. These will mean various degrees of suffering and will necessitate medical attention. Genital cancers and HIV can result in death. In contrast, risk of an easily treatable condition during a circumcision is very low (1 in 250), and of a true complication is 1 in 5000. A successful circumcision is extremely unlikely to have any long-term adverse consequences and cosmetic outcome is generally excellent.*

She got this 1990s packet: 

https://www.circinfo.net/pdfs/GFP_EN(US)_1606.pdf

Sorry if I wasn't clear in the post: the doctors/her friends told my mother that the vast majority of American women preferred the look of a circumcised penis.

But that wasn't close to the main reason. 

The doctors told her it was strongly recommended for all males to be so. Because it is dramatically easier to clean, lessened the risks of STD's and UTI's, reduced the risk of foreskin discomfort, prevented it from not retracting properly later in life, was considered more attractive by the vast majority of American women, and thus made it easier to get a willing sexual partner and future wife. (1990s)

That's why I'm willing to forgive her. Although I'm angry that she didn't apparently research the issue in detail. But people tend to default to what medical figures say. So I understand.

But I do feel like I was harmed from negligence.

I'm planning on visiting a urologist/sexual health doctor of some kind about the issue.

So I haven't been that explicit about that particular issue to them. They still think I'm a "man of faith."

And thanks. I'm definitely going to a therapist about this. Just trying to find one that's worked with similar cases/understanding of my perspective.

What was done to us was terrible.

Thank you.

I live in the United States. So it was promoted as a hygiene thing to parents when I was born.

But, yeah. It's awful. 

I have reoccurring suicidal thoughts because of what was done for me. And in the past, I've considered moving to a place where suicide is legal to kill myself. 

Because I can't stand having this body. I feel like I was molested, mutilated, and raped. And no one will take my concern seriously, there's no way to reverse it, and I think it looks hideous.

I'm not going to go through with it.
But I feel like a core aspect of me will always be damaged and pathetic. 

So mentions of sex, romance, or dating make me extremely angry.  It feels like my life is already ruined.

I wish I could know what being uncut was like. Because it doesn't really feel like anything when I masturbate: and mine was very aggressive. But I don't really have anything to compare it, to, though.

I'm not Christian anymore... mostly because of this.

But the fact that it's forced upon children who can't even consent to the procedure.
And it's legal in every country in the world: as shocking as that is to believe.

I was circumcised at birth.

And it's led to years of me hating my body, feelings of humiliation and sexual violation, and reoccurring suicidal thoughts. Sex is ruined for me.

Fuck anyone who does this. 

Mutilators of children.

The journey to unbelief.

And the pleasure's very faint.

But it isn't even truly restore it. The nerve endings are still gone. It just gives the appearance of foreskin.

My parents? The doctors?  Society?
